title: Desk Guidance: Patient Payment Plan Schedule and Next Due Date on a Re-age
content:
On a **Patient Payment Plan** re-age, the installments moved to the end of the schedule are the consecutive missed installments the plan records, and the re-aged schedule length is the plan's current number of scheduled installments plus the installments moved, never longer than the longest re-aged schedule, which is the tier's maximum term, and never shorter than the current number of scheduled installments.

**Next due date.** A re-age settles every missed installment the plan records, so the plan's next due date moves forward one month, on the plan's due day, for each missed installment the plan recorded.

**Order.** The installments moved are counted first and added to the current number of scheduled installments, the longest re-aged schedule is applied to that sum next, and the rule that the schedule is never left shorter than the current one is applied last.

### Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

| Current scheduled installments | Missed installments recorded | Tier maximum term | Re-aged schedule length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 2 | 36 | 22 |
| 35 | 3 | 36 | 36 (held to the maximum term) |
| 40 | 2 | 36 | 40 (never shorter than the current schedule) |

On the first row, a plan due on the 1st whose next due date is 1 March and which records 2 missed installments has its next due date moved to 1 May.
